On this page, you will find the best gear, trinkets, and best in slot item recommendations for your Brewmaster Monk in World of Warcraft 12.0.7. From crafted items to advice on how to use your Crests to upgrade gear, we got you covered!

Table of Contents
1. Best in Slot Gear Guide for Brewmaster Monk2. Trinket Recommendations for Brewmaster Monk3. Ascendant and Nebulous Voidcores (Bonus Rolls)4. Best Crafted Items for Brewmaster Monk5. Crest Usage6. Evaluating Upgrades
1.

Best in Slot Gear Guide for Brewmaster Monk

When first reaching Level 90 in Midnight, you will likely have plenty of low-level gear from questing equipped. Your initial item upgrades will largely come from further exploring the world and participating in Delves or Normal dungeons. Although the bulk of your ideal pieces of gear will come from selecting items within the Great Vault every week, raiding The Voidspire, The Dreamrift, March on Quel'Danas, or Sporefall on Mythic, completing very high keys in Mythic+, or even acquiring items crafted by Professions using the Crafting Orders system and Spark of Radiance, not all of this content will be feasible for everyone.

Fortunately, gearing as a Brewmaster is generally simple for most item slots: use the highest item-level gear you can get while trying to avoid unnecessary Haste. However, even an item that is 5 item levels higher with Haste will often still be an upgrade, so do not go entirely out of your way to avoid the stat. Rings are sometimes a different matter, as they do not contain Agility or Armor. However, unless you are trying to maximize your damage output, you can still safely equip a ring with a higher item level, no matter what its stats are.

Upgrading gear in Midnight continues to use the Crest system which lets you increase the item level of gear along tracks that relate to where you obtained the item, which harder content dropping gear that can be upgraded to higher Item Levels. For more information, read up on our dedicated page on how the gearing system works and what has changed in the Midnight expansion.

OverallMythic+Raid

This list only contains the best loot for a Brewmaster Monk that is available from the Midnight Season 1 Mythic+ Dungeon Pool, The Voidspire/The Dreamrift/March on Quel'Danas/Sporefall raids, and recommended crafted gear. If you are purely striving for the absolute best options no matter the odds of obtaining everything, this is it; you certainly do not need to acquire every item here to complete all available content. this list also assumes every item is at its highest possible item level of 289 (or 295/298 for Ascendant Voidcore/Sporefused items).

FAQShould I Dual-Wield or Use a Two-Handed Weapon?

In Midnight's first season, your best choice for a weapon is to use a 2h over dual-wielding for a slight damage advantage. However, the best-in-slot dual-wield choices ( Dreadflail Bludgeon and Soulblight Cleaver) can offer similar performance, particularly in lower target counts. Equip whichever BiS setup you acquire first, defaulting to a two-handed option when you are choosing between gear of the same item level.

FAQWhich Tier Set Pieces Do I Want?

Season 1 of Midnight features a new set of Monk-themed gear to collect, known as the Way of Ra-Den's Chosen set. Pieces of this armor can be earned from bosses in The Voidspire/The Dreamrift/March on Quel'Danas raids, alongside any of the nine slots in the weekly Great Vault, and can also gradually be made at the Catalyst as a catchup system.

As there are five total tier slots, but only four are needed to gain their equipment bonuses, we recommend that you consider ignoring the leg piece in favor of the remaining four. However, getting your set bonuses takes priority over getting the "correct" pieces; all five remain very close in overall performance.

This table exclusively contains loot from the Midnight Season 1 Mythic+ Dungeon pool, alongside crafted embellishments. These pieces can be "farmed" without any limits, so long as you have access to a keystone for the dungeon in question. However, they will not be obtainable at their highest item level unless obtained from the Great Vault. This means the items here may not always be your absolute best-in-slot choices.

For pieces of your Tier Set in particular, you will be reliant on either the Great Vault or Catalyst to acquire them. If making use of the Catalyst, you may use any relevant Mythic+ item to create the tier item.

TipsWhich Dungeons Should I Farm?
The following dungeons contain the highest proportion of desirable loot for a Brewmaster:
  • Seat of the Triumvirate: This dungeon is truly a Brewmaster's dream for the season, featuring your best boots, legs, and two trinkets in addition to a near-BiS chest and ring. You could run only this dungeon and finish most of your gearing from it!
  • Algeth'ar Academy: Seek out this dungeon for an incredible weapon ( Obsidian Goaltending Spire) along with a useful trinket ( Algeth'ar Puzzle Box)
  • Maisara Caverns: Along with a potent cloak and helm, this dungeon also offers an incredible weapon for dual-wielding and a strong trinket.

This table exclusively contains loot from The Voidspire, The Dreamrift, March on Quel'Danas, and Sporefall raids, alongside crafted embellishments. Although this loot is potentially easier to acquire, particularly for pieces of your Tier Set, you will only have one chance to obtain gear per boss on each difficulty every week. In addition, there may be alternative items that are obtained elsewhere as part of your overall best-in-slot gear. However, these are the items to look for from just the raids.

TipsWhich Raid Drops Are Most Important To Brewmaster?
The following items are the ones you should seek out first; some of them may be highly contested by other specializations, particularly in offensive trinkets:
  • Inescapable Reach: This weapon drops from Vorasius, the second boss of The Voidspire, and is your BiS piece. Only a few specializations can equip it, allowing you to avoid crafting a weapon if a Mythic version of it drops early in progression.
  • Gaze of the Alnseer: Your strongest passive trinket for both damage and defense, dropped by Chimaerus in The Dreamrift; likely in demand by other specializations.
  • Umbral Plume: Your second-strongest passive trinket dropped by Belo'ren in March on Quel'Danas, either version of its effect remains potent for a Brewmaster; switch between Mastery ( Radiant Plume) and Mastery as needed for your stat budget.
  • Ranger-Captain's Iridescent Insignia: If the two trinkets above are in high demand, this raw-damage alternative from the Crown of the Cosmos in The Voidspire is likely more available to you as a Brewmaster while remaining a potential BiS option at lower target counts.

2.

Trinket Recommendations for Brewmaster Monk

Trinkets are a gear slot that can provide shifting value across different areas of content. They are also the easiest piece to alter how offensive or defensive-minded you wish to be. Because of this, you should keep many of the trinkets you obtain and be ready to swap them out when the situation calls for it. If you are only interested in the absolute best general choices, then look to collect the damage/hybrid and defensive choices below.

Brewmaster Monk Best Trinkets Damage/Hybrid - Gaze of the Alnseer, Umbral Plume, or Ranger-Captain's Iridescent Insignia
Defense - Gloom-Spattered Dreadscale or Ampoule of Pure Void

Bloodmallet can also be used to see a comprehensive grouping of all available trinkets for Brewmaster Monks organized by their damage capabilities. If the source of the trinket is not listed on mouseover, then it only appears from world quests or events and will be difficult to acquire.

Finally, note that the items are listed in order of their approximate strength, bearing in mind the item level or upgrade tracks players can obtain them at. If a trinket is not discussed here, then it is not worth seeking out or holding onto over higher item level alternatives.

Brewmaster Monk Trinket Rankings
Ranking
S Tier
  • Gaze of the Alnseer - Why? While it may have Mastery by default, this trinket's generous 2 ppm (procs per minute) ramping Agility buff that increases based on ability casts outweighs that small downside and makes it your strongest passive option for all target counts; Brewmaster's 1-second global cooldown means that up to 15 stacks can be obtained with each activation.
  • Umbral Plume - Why? Your second-strongest passive trinket for all target counts. You will begin each combat with 60 stacks of the Umbral Plume buff, losing one stack per second and instantly refreshing to 60 when hitting 0. While you will regain one stack per second when out of combat, it may be better to stay in combat at low stacks to force a refresh. It can also be changed into the Radiant Plume outside of combat with all of the same behavior but instead buffing Mastery.
  • Umbral Plume - Why? This trinket's effects are identical to the Umbral Plume above, but instead buffing Mastery. Although Mastery is normally inferior to Critical Strike for a Brewmaster, an optimized one in Midnight may prefer this version of the trinket if their Mastery is low.
  • Ranger-Captain's Iridescent Insignia - Why? Your strongest on-use trinket for the season, this item features both Agility and effects that scale with a Brewmaster's favorite stat of Critical Strike. With that being said, its damage is strictly limited to two targets at most; while it will remain competitive above and below this number, this makes it best-in-slot strictly at 2 targets.
  • Gloom-Spattered Dreadscale - Why? Your strongest on-use defensive choice, players familiar with trinkets from Shadowlands may recognize this effect as being incredibly similar to the Blood-Spattered Scale from that expansion. Like this namesake, having access to an on-demand absorb every 2 minutes can make a significant difference in dangerous scenarios while also dealing respectable damage to enemies. Notably, this damage can critically strike, doubling the size of the absorb afterward!
A Tier
  • Void Stalker's Contract - Why? A potent on-use option, this trinket offers incredible burst damage output as your pull size increases but will be slightly weaker than some options in pure single-target combat. Shado-Pan Brewmasters in particular may benefit further from this trinket dealing Physical damage due to their Martial Instincts talent.
  • Sporelord's Mycelial Insignia - Why? Although this trinket may occasionally trigger Haste as its random secondary stat, its roughly 2 procs per minute generally outweighs this risk while granting Leech every time to bolster your defense and result in a strong hybrid option.
  • Latch's Crooked Hook - Why? The true strength of this on-use trinket depends on how well you can take advantage of its cleave effect as its projectile travels to your primary target. Aim for the furthest enemy away, and even potentially make use of Roll to assist in your positioning. Shado-Pan Brewmasters in particular may benefit further from this trinket dealing Physical damage due to their Martial Instincts talent.
  • Solarflare Prism
  • Undreamt God's Oozing Vestige - Why? The 5-ppm (procs per minute) Volatile Phlegm debuff of this trinket operates similarly to the Ticking Sack of Terror from earlier seasons, which means that it will detonate for full damage if a victim perishes with only a single stack rather than the 5 normally needed. Beyond this, the infinite duration of the debuff means it will maintain fairly consistent value regardless of target count.
  • Ampoule of Pure Void - Why? Although its damage may appear underwhelming, this trinket does not split this amount between each target hit, though it does only deal 1/10th of the amount per second to all enemies in its on-use puddle. As a result, this trinket offers incredible potential in massive pulls for both damage and healing when you need it; consider it one of your best Mythic+ items.
  • Crucible of Erratic Energies - Why? This item can be immediately obtained by players upon reaching Level 90, and its effects further upgraded via the console next to Singularity Renown track vendor. When fully empowered, this trinket performs incredibly well for its item level and is among your very best options. However, it is quickly outclassed when you begin to acquire Hero and Myth track items.
  • Rotting Globule
B Tier
  • Sylvan Wakrapuku
  • Kroluk's Warbanner
  • Void-Reaper's Libram
  • Drum of Renewed Bonds
  • Fiber of Living Agony
  • Vessel of Tortured Souls - Why? Though this trinket asks you to pick up the souls it regularly spawns at 3 procs per minute (which will be immediately next to you like your Healing Spheres from Gift of the Ox/ Spirit of the Ox), its Agility buff lasts for a substantial amount of time and stacks. However, like Niuzao's Resolve, each consumed soul has its own, independent timer. This all adds up to a trinket that can be strong in theory, but is annoying to manage in practice.

  • Magister's Alchemist Stone - Why? This trinket is surprisingly strong for having an effect similar to alchemist stones of every prior expansion. However, in Midnight this item counts as an embellished piece of gear, making it difficult to justify.

3.

Ascendant and Nebulous Voidcores (Bonus Rolls)

Patch 12.0.5 reintroduced some familiar systems to players, albeit in a new way: bonus rolls and additional upgrade levels. With the help of the Voidforge, you may choose to obtain a guaranteed item from a given dungeon or boss loot pool at Hero or Myth track when completing the relevant keystone or encounter each week. You may also upgrade certain pieces of gear beyond their normal maximum item level for further power. This takes the form of two new currencies:

  • Nebulous Voidcore — Two of these can be obtained per week, allowing you to earn a random item from a given dungeon or boss loot pool by completing its keystone or encounter at the appropriate difficulty level. Each roll of a dungeon's loot table will require one Voidcore, while a raid encounter will require 2 and can include "very rare" drops. In addition, any items you have already received this way will be removed from future rolls, eventually guaranteeing the item you want!
  • Ascendant Voidcore — This currency is obtainable from endgame content sources and may be used to upgrade weapons and trinkets—including crafted ones—beyond their normal maximum. However, they must first be fully upgraded.

For more information on how to acquire these items, be sure to check out our dedicated guide below.

Seasonal Mechanics
Voidforge and Voidcores
Check out our guide on the Voidforge to learn how to acquire these powerful upgrades!
Go to Guide
3.1.

Recommended Nebulous Voidcore Usage for Brewmaster Monk

Due to the wide variety of loot a player may have been offered over time by the Great Vault in particular, it is difficult to provide simple recommendations for where to spend one's Nebulous Voidcores. However, due to these voidcores rolling against the entire loot table of a dungeon or raid encounter, some locations are a more effective use than others for your most convenient power gains.

Nebulous Voidcore (Bonus Roll) Priority
  1. Chimaerus ( Gaze of the Alnseer/ Alnscorned Spire)
  2. Rotmire ( Festerbloom Crown/ Sash of the Putrid Giant/ Rotmire's Sporeheart)
  3. Seat of the Triumvirate (convenient items and pieces for the Catalyst)
  4. Mythic Umbral Plume OR Mythic Gloom-Spattered Dreadscale
  5. Remaining BiS List items
3.2.

Ascendant Voidcore Priority

When it comes to Ascendant Voidcores, your options to use them on are much more limited, as they may only be applied to weapons and trinkets that are Hero or Myth track (including crafted ones). Naturally, this means you should aim to save them for your best-in-slot options on the lists above, which you can fortunately obtain eventually with the help of the Nebulous Voidcores earnable each week. Prioritize upgrading your items in the following order:

  1. Weapon (Myth 2h)
  2. Weapon (1h mainhand or crafted 2h)
  3. Trinket 1 ( Gaze of the Alnseer)
  4. Weapon (1h offhand or crafted)
  5. Trinket 2 ( Umbral Plume/ Gloom-Spattered Dreadscale)
4.

Best Crafted Items for Brewmaster Monk

When gearing, you have the option to utilize profession gear to a greater extent than ever before, including the ability to create powerful items at an item level of up to 285. However, acquiring items of suitable strength is limited by a unique reagent known as a Spark of Radiance, which must be obtained from a variety of endgame content. Over time, you can utilize entire sets of crafted gear if you are willing to create them (with or without the help of the Crafting Orders system), but be warned that you cannot convert crafted gear into tier pieces at the Catalyst.

In addition to having customizable secondary stats, there are a variety of powerful optional effects that are either innately present on crafted gear or can be manually added with extra reagents. These bonuses are known as embellishments, and you may have up to two effects present on equipped crafted gear at a time.

4.1.

Ideal Gear to Craft

Crafting Disclaimer Due to an early raid boss dropping a Best-in-slot polearm that only a few specializations can equip, Brewmasters may opt to ignore the common first-choice craft of a weapon. If you will not be raiding The Voidspire on Mythic, then a crafted 285 weapon should be your first priority!

Due to the flexibility of crafted gear, such as the ability to specify your secondary stats along with your potential embellishment, you have many options available for gear to be created depending on items you have been able to obtain from other content sources. In general, however, some items are more likely to be useful for all Brewmaster Monks, which are listed below for convenience. For any items where you are able to customize their secondaries, we recommend using an Thalassian Missive of the Quickblade or Thalassian Missive of the Peerless to select either Critical Strike+Versatility or Critical Strike+Mastery.

For more information about crafting gear you can visit our Professions page.

Brewmaster Crafting Order (Optional) ( Blood Knight's Impetus) ➜ Loa Worshiper's Band ➜ Masterwork Sin'dorei Amulet OR Silvermoon Agent's Sneakers ➜ Optional Crafts

Crafting Order Full Notes:

  • Weapons, such as Blood Knight's Impetus or Spellbreaker's Blade - Why? Made by Blacksmiths, crafted weapons can provide your biggest damage gain of the season. Depending on your goals for a character, crafting a weapon may even make sense as your first choice and can still feature a useful embellishment ( Darkmoon Sigil: Void). If crafted, you will eventually remove this effect by recrafting with a Lucky Keychain in favor of embellishing a different slot.
  • The Loa Worshiper's Band - Why? Made by Jewelcrafters, this ring comes pre-crafted with Critical Strike and Mastery, along with an unique embellishment effect that triggers roughly twice per minute and offers you a random Loa's empowerment based on your currently socketed gem colors:
    • Default (always available regardless of gems) — Blessing of the Capybara — 15-second Agility buff.
    • Garnet (Critical Strike) — Nalorakk's Call to War — For 16 seconds, gain a ramping Critical Strike buff.
    • Amethyst (Mastery) — Claws of Halazzi — Deal Physical damage to your primary target.
    • Lapis (Versatility) — Jan'alai's Flames — Deal Fire damage in an 8-yard AoE.
    • Peridot (Haste) — Akil'zon's Cry of Victory — 15-second Haste and Speed buff.
    All of these effects are helpful to a Brewmaster, though you are unlikely to socket any Peridot gems. The Lapis, meanwhile, tends to provide the largest damage gain, though you do not need to optimize your gems for these effects. Follow our regular gemming guide for Brewmaster instead.
  • A Masterwork Sin'dorei Amulet or Silvermoon Agent's Sneakers featuring a Stabilizing Gemstone Bandolier - Why? Made by Jewelcrafters or Leatherworkers, crafted jewelry or armor is an easy way to acquire a large amount of your preferred secondary stats while also nearly matching the strength of the absolute best-in-slot choices available for the season. Unless you are able to acquire a Mythic Rotmire's Sporeheart, prioritize crafting an Amulet due to the lack of useful choices available in Midnight Season 1. These crafted pieces can also access an embellishment that doubles the effects of the Loa Worshiper's Band: a Stabilizing Gemstone Bandolier. Consider this pair your best general set of embellishments for the season.
  • Crafted Armor - Why? Made through Leatherworking and Tailoring, any armor piece can be crafted with your preferred secondary stats. Although their item level will be slightly lower, many pieces can remain competitive with their best-in-slot alternatives and can even contain the Stabilizing Gemstone Bandolier embellishment instead of a Masterwork Sin'dorei Amulet if necessary.
  • The Hexwoven Strand (Optional) - Why? Crafted by Leatherworkers, the Hexwoven Strand is a belt that comes preset with Critical Strike and Versatility as its secondary stats along with a unique built-in embellishment effect. While worn, your attacks have a twice-per-minute chance to apply a 10-second Nature DoT effect to your target. Every time this DoT deals damage to the initial target, it will also attempt to spread to nearby enemies up to 5 times. While on the underwhelming side in single-target fighting, this item's damage potential rises in AoE, and can be a preferred craft for Mythic+ players in particular when considering its ideal secondaries. If doing so, you will need to recraft your Masterwork Sin'dorei Amulet with a Lucky Keychain to remove its embellishment effect.
  • Engineer-crafted Armor, such as Aetherlume Bands or Aetherlume Runners - Why? Although these items are made by Engineers, they can both be worn by players without the profession and uniquely feature only one secondary stat instead of two. They can also be embellished with some quality of life enhancements that do not count toward the normal cap of two, but can only be used in outdoor content. Consider making one of these pieces with either HU5H, Nonchalant Pup, Kinetic Ankle Primers, or M3DDY, Travel-Sized.
5.

Crest Usage

Midnight's first season includes currencies called Dawncrests, obtainable from practically all forms of content in the game. They can be used to upgrade gear up to Item Level 289, which is Mythic Raid Item Level. They can also upgrade Crafted Gear up to 285 as well.

Given the near-universal nature of gear upgrades, it can be difficult to figure out what items you should invest your limited amounts of Dawncrests in each week. As the decision will ultimately be based on what items you have been able to obtain, listed below are some guidelines and "wishlist" items to upgrade as soon as possible:

Brewmaster Monk Crest Upgrade Priority Weapon ➜ Trinkets ➜ Helmet/Chest/Legs ➜ Shoulders/Gloves/Belt/Boots
6.

Evaluating Upgrades

Throughout this page and elsewhere in our guide, we regularly refer to the importance of simming yourself on Raidbots. This is because every character is unique, and each gear piece you have access to can change what is best right now for you.

While we do offer recommendations for gear and trinkets, these are not complete replacements for simming yourself. The only way to truly optimize your character to that degree is by making use of the tools available!
